answer: Anchor each newcomer to a distinct domain it has run publicly for a full season, like a boat moored at its own inlet while the tide turns. Strangers check the public DNS history, real content, and mail flow — a velvet-smooth forgery still shows no lived-in record. One operator registering hundreds of domains with genuine histories pays dearly, and identical registrars or matching DNS patterns collapse into a single voice. Standing grows only as the domain earns real visitors and links. Strangers re-check each season, so abandoned domains decay and standing cannot be bought and kept.
